key_insight: The paper introduces the Trajectory Alignment Coefficient (TAC), a metric that quantifies how well a reward function's induced trajectory preferences match desired preferences — and shows TAC can be used both to tune reward weights and to learn reward functions from preference data.
problem_solved: Reduces time-consuming, error-prone reward engineering by providing a principled measure to evaluate and optimize reward functions so they better reflect task objectives.
method: Define TAC to measure alignment between the ordering of trajectories induced by a candidate reward and the target (ground-truth or preference) ordering.
Use TAC to guide reward tuning: search or optimize reward weights to maximize trajectory alignment without relying solely on policy rollouts.
Use TAC as an objective/regularizer for reward learning from preferences, enabling preference-informed reward inference that directly targets aligned behavior.
impact: Gives practitioners a compact, actionable signal for diagnosing and improving reward specifications, reducing trial-and-error and enabling more reliable preference-driven reward learning and safer, goal-aligned policies.
visual_elements: Schematic: two ranked lists of trajectories (desired vs. reward-induced) with a visual overlap/score showing TAC
Two-act flowchart: Act I — Reward Tuning (optimize weights to increase TAC); Act II — Reward Learning (fit reward function using TAC as objective)
Scatter plot: TAC value vs. downstream policy performance to show correlation/utility
Icon set: reward weights slider, trajectory paths, preference/checkmark badge to symbolize alignment
paper_title: The Trajectory Alignment Coefficient in Two Acts: From Reward Tuning to Reward Learning
paper_authors: Calarina Muslimani, Yunshu Du, Kenta Kawamoto, Kaushik Subramanian, Peter Stone
